text.p: The International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers said it filed a $200 million libel suit against Walt Disney Co. Monday, saying the film "Ransom" injured the union's reputation.
The lawsuit, filed in state circuit court in Prince Georges County, also named Richard Price and Alexander Ignon, the script's co-writers, as defendants.
The union is seeking $50 million in compensatory damages and $150 million in punitive damages.

An attorney for the machinists, John Walsh, said the union was unfairly portrayed as corrupt in the film, which stars Mel Gibson as the wealthy owner of an airline whose son is kidnapped and held for a $2 million ransom.

"A key role in the movie's plot is that of a person clearly described as a corrupt 'Machinists union' official, a description which is accompanied by references to 'Machinists union indictments,'" said Walsh.
Since the movie's Nov. 2 release, he said there have been hundreds of inquiries and expressions of concern from union members and the general public about the references.
